newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end sharply up on reshuffle news.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end sharply up on reshuffle news.

text.p: Taiwan stocks closed sharply up on Wednesday as confidence was boosted after President Lee Teng-hui called for a cabinet reshuffle, showing the government's determination to crack down on crime problems, brokers said.
The weighted index jumped 132.80 points, or 1.60 percent, to finish at 8,427.07 points. Turnover was a sizzling T$107.4 billion.

"The market was quick to react to the reshuffle news. It shows the government has realised the seriousness of the social disorder and (is) willing to improve the situation," said Amy Huang, an analyst of Nomura Securities.

Premier Lien Chan tendered his resignation on Sunday to take responsibility for the government's failure to check violent crime, an issue which came under intense scrutiny following the murder of the daughter of a popular actress.
Lien's resignation was rejected. But Lee asked Lien to "make some adjustments" in cabinet positions and resolve the gruesome murder case as soon as possible.
High-technology shares attracted strong buying interest on hopes of sound profit outlooks, brokers said.
The most active issue, United Micro, surged T$4 or 6.06 percent to T$70.
